graphEvents.label: Approval not bound to executed plan

label: Partial decisions in a conflict unit silently drop the release changes of every undecided file: prepareWrites marks the unit applied once any file is decided (release-update.cjs:1691-1718) and records the release tree as that unit's base (1728-1731), so an undecided conflict file reads local-only (648) and the unit reads quiet 'local' (916). Reproduced: decide b.md only, apply exits 0, a.md stays pre-release and re-check reports local-only. Align keeps partial runs on failure (align.yaml:125) and apply has no completeness check (apply.yaml:96). Untested.

The interrupted-apply stale lock reported by iterations 1, 2 and 5 is one defect and is broader than claimed: Node runs no finally on SIGTERM or SIGINT (probe: lock survived both), so Ctrl-C or a tool-timeout kill strands .skilled/release/.apply.lock (release-update.cjs:1775-1794, 1903-1905), whose recorded pid is never read back; rollback needs the same lock (2035) and the workflow forbids removing it (apply.yaml:98,131). A kill inside writeAtomic also strands a <target>.release-update-<pid>-<ts> temp file (1809-1821).

Copied or vendored trees cannot reach the framework upstream through /doctor:update: the engine defaults --remote to origin (release-update.cjs:2073) but the router and workflows expose no --remote (update.md:3,36-38; check.yaml:34-40), and the presentation's record-base command omits it (presentation.txt:86). Probe: a vendored copy without a framework origin reports upstream unknown and unit blocked/none; with --remote it reports update/inferred. All vendored tests pass --remote (test.cjs:545,1197).

The single startup approval is not bound to the executed plan: apply --dry-run returns no release or runDir (release-update.cjs:1860-1873; probe keys confirm) although the plan template shows both (presentation.txt:191-193), and a no-decisions apply re-plans from a fresh check whose release is upstream latest at call time (1554-1561, 751). A tag published between dry-run and approval changes the release written without re-approval, contrary to command-contract.json:244; local edits in that window are refused, not overwritten (1644-1661).

A second apply is refused until the operator commits base.json, and no workflow or result template says to commit: apply's HEAD-dirty check covers its own ledgers (release-update.cjs:1733-1760). Reproduced on the documented journey apply update units, then align and apply --decisions: exit 1 'target has staged or unstaged changes against HEAD: .skilled/release/base.json'. Tests commit between applies (test.cjs:932,979).

A bare apply after align consumes the alignment run and discards its decisions: resolveApplyRun reuses the newest unapplied run at HEAD with an empty decision set (release-update.cjs:1566-1571), writes rollback.json into it (1889), and the run is then 'already applied' (1830-1832). Reproduced: bare apply ran in the align run directory, then apply --decisions on that run exited 1. Documented at apply.yaml:46 but never warned.

The base-recording prompt never clears on a copied tree: after record-base and a commit, check still reports baseRecording.needed for directory:release, the engine's own .skilled/release directory enumerated as a unit (release-update.cjs:535), and for any unit new in the release (test.cjs:569 asserts this). record-base records only release units (1981), so following presentation.txt:82-88 cannot satisfy it. Reproduced.

record-base trusts the operator-named release without comparing it to the local tree (release-update.cjs:1996-2001) although check already computes that distance (820-835); naming a later release than installed makes its changed files read local-only (648) so the update never lands (inference, not reproduced). It also writes base.json without the apply lock (2003 vs 1875).

An explicit --release older than the recorded base plans a silent downgrade labelled update: local equals base gives take-release (release-update.cjs:647) and an all-take-release unit is 'update' (919); nothing compares the release to the base release (inference from code, not reproduced).

Rollback and record-base have no route: the router accepts only check, align and apply (update.md:35; presentation.txt:10-11); rollback is reachable only inside the apply battery (apply.yaml:177-181), so after a session ends or an interruption the engine error points at a raw command (release-update.cjs:1899-1901) with no approval, validator or state log; sk-create-command asks for recovery design (SKILL.md:378).

Remaining Q1 field drift: check promises upstream_status available|unknown|offline (check.yaml:79) but the engine emits known|unknown (release-update.cjs:744,771); no workflow maps engine status current|updates-available|blocked|unknown (1092-1100) to STATUS=OK|UNKNOWN|FAILED; rollback exit 1 on skipped paths (2060) is undocumented; regenerateHubs holds hub names (1946) while the battery takes <hub-dir> (apply.yaml:137-138); apply cannot pass --offline or --remote (update.md:38) though the engine accepts them (51-54). Exit codes, kind:name keys, lock acquisition and rollback.json ordering match.

followUps.regenerate is displayed but never acted on: apply.yaml:56 lists it and presentation.txt:201 shows generators, but no battery step runs or checks the trigger-index generator (release-update.cjs:78; apply.yaml:133-176); it refreshes only if the operator accepts the optional /doctor:rebuild (doctor-rebuild.yaml:170).

Iteration 1 confirmed: align and apply user_inputs omit include_prerelease (align.yaml:33-38; apply.yaml:37-42) while check declares it (check.yaml:40) and the router binds only declared inputs (update.md:50).
Iteration 1 confirmed: the router carries base-recording next-step wording (update.md:68) that the presentation owns (presentation.txt:82-88; sk-create-command SKILL.md:354).
Iteration 2 confirmed as a code path, not reproduced: binary detection is NUL or invalid UTF-8 only (release-update.cjs:555-560).

Iteration 2 confirmed: the generated inventory is a closed list (release-update.cjs:79-100) and no test touches trigger-index patterns. Narrowed doc claim: update.md:66 says apply names generators instead of writing generated files, but reclassification applies only to local-only or conflict (701-707), so a release change to an unregenerated artifact is take-release and apply writes it.
Iteration 2 confirmed: renames are joined by exact path with no rename test (release-update.cjs:1015-1058).

Iteration 2 narrowed: offline plus a tagless vendor fails closed (probe: blocked, base none), but the claim that the vendored path works when a remote is reachable holds only for the raw engine with --remote or a framework origin; the routed command fails the same way online (see f-iter006-003).

Iteration 3 confirmed: cancellation and interruption map to STATUS=DECLINED (presentation.txt:212) with no cancelled status (apply.yaml:197-203), against STATUS=CANCELLED ACTION=cancelled (sk-create-command SKILL.md:379).

Iteration 3 confirmed: apply says dry_run_writes_nothing (apply.yaml:33) yet writes a state log on dry-run (apply.yaml:111); align writes none on dry-run (align.yaml:138), so the two workflows disagree.
Iteration 3 confirmed: the canonical doctor argument_hint omits --include-prerelease (command-contract.json:203) while the router hint has it (update.md:3).
Iteration 3 confirmed, low impact: Grep and Glob are granted (update.md:4) but used by no router or workflow step (sk-create-command SKILL.md:218-219).

Iteration 3 narrowed: the check workflow does disclose the git fetch exception (check.yaml:16-23) and the router summary says without changing checkout files (update.md:64); only update.md:16 and the presentation omit the qualifier.

Iteration 4 confirmed and widened: test.cjs:832-838 applies a prefilled adopt-release with no decide call, and the claim that the routed workflow closes the acceptance gate fails for an interrupted align, whose partial run apply accepts (see f-iter006-001).

Iteration 4 narrowed: a tree-less base record is accepted (release-update.cjs:806) but every current writer records a tree (1730, 1999), and the fingerprint guards only against a moved tag, never against a wrongly named release (see f-iter006-008).
Iteration 4 invariant confirmed: align writes only under its run directory (release-update.cjs:1371-1382), and the engine suite passes 56/56.

Iteration 5 narrowed: the changelog index is stale (changelog/skilled/README.md:23-25 while v4.0.0.3.md exists), but the engine identifies releases from git tags (release-update.cjs:389-392) and never reads the index, so the impact is docs only.

Iteration 5 copied-tree acquisition documentation finding was not re-read this pass; f-iter006-003 sharpens it, because the copied-tree route also needs a framework remote the routed command cannot name.
